Product Lane Settings customise the investigation workflow, filtering options, and categorisation for each product/type combination.

Issue types are categories used when investigating test failures — labels like Defect, Automation Issue, or Environment that describe why a test failed. They appear when you open a failing test and click Investigate. Issue types are configured at two levels: 1. Global Issue Types (System Settings) — defined once, available system-wide. Go to Settings → System Settings → Global Issue Types. Add types with Key, Label, Icon, and Color. 2. Product Lane Issue Types — each lane selects which global types to expose in its investigation dropdown. Edit a Product Lane → Issue Types section → add from Available Types. Default issue types available in all lanes: Type When to use Defect A product bug caused the failure — a real regression Automation Issue The test itself is broken (selector, timing, test-code bug), not the product tip Keep global issue types generic (Defect, Automation Issue, Environment) and add product-specific types at the Product Lane level.

Useful when you have many teams or components and want to analyse at a higher level. A Preset is a named, saved set of product-lane filter combinations. Instead of manually adding lanes one by one each time you open the product-lane selector, save a multi-lane view as a preset and reload it in one click. Presets are especially useful for cross-browser or cross-environment comparisons you run regularly — e.g. a preset called "All Browsers" that always adds Chrome, Firefox, and Safari lanes at once.

Go to Settings → Presets (admin or operator) Click Add Preset — enter a name and optional description Add lanes — each lane is a combination of: Dimension Notes product Required per lane type Required per lane version Optional browser Optional platform Optional platform_version Optional team Optional stage Optional device Optional The UI validates that each lane exists in UReport before adding it. If a combination matches multiple lanes or none at all, the entry is rejected. Click Save

Open the product-lane selector (available in the Launches page and the widget editor). In the selector dropdown, choose from the Presets list. All lanes defined in the preset are instantly applied, replacing any currently selected lanes. info Applying a preset replaces the current lane selection. To keep existing lanes, add them individually before or after applying a preset.

Instantly understand why any test failed — root cause category, confidence score, plain-English explanation, and a suggested fix, powered by the LLM provider of your choice.

When a test fails, click Analyse with AI in the test detail panel. UReport sends the error message, stack trace, step context, and prior run history to your configured LLM. The model returns: Output Description Root Cause Category One of six categories — see Root Cause Categories below Confidence Score 0–100% confidence in the category. Low scores indicate ambiguous failures worth reviewing manually. Explanation Plain-English description of what likely went wrong and why, based on the error and execution context Suggested Fix Actionable recommendation — a config change, code fix, or environment check Flakiness Signal One of four values: consistent, intermittent, regression, or new. Signals the failure pattern observed across runs — useful for distinguishing a brand-new failure from a recurring flaky test. Related Patterns String array of patterns identified across similar failures in the same suite — surfaces common error themes so you can address systemic issues info The Analyse with AI button is only shown for failed tests. Passed and skipped tests do not have an Analyse option.

Results are cached by error fingerprint (a hash of the error message and stack trace). If ten tests share the same failure, only the first triggers an LLM call — the rest receive the cached result instantly at no extra cost.

When a test is analysed, UReport checks all other tests in the same build that share the exact same error message and stack trace. Those siblings are immediately marked as analysed with the same result, without triggering additional LLM calls. Clicking "Analyse with AI" on one test can resolve dozens of identical failures at once.

When a failing test has steps, the LLM receives a window of steps centred on the failed step: the 5 steps immediately before the failure and the 3 steps immediately after. This gives the model both the lead-up and any cleanup/teardown context without bloating the prompt with the entire test run. tip Submitting steps via your reporter significantly improves analysis quality. Without steps, the model only sees the error message and stack trace.

After viewing the AI result, you can: Confirm — agree with the root cause category Override — select the correct category if the AI was wrong Feedback is recorded per analysis. Over time, this data lets you track how accurate the AI is for your specific test suite and identify where the model needs improvement.

Go to Settings → AI Analysis (admin only) Choose a provider: Provider Credential required Notes AWS Bedrock (Claude) AWS access key + secret + region Recommended for enterprise — stays within your AWS boundary Anthropic Claude API Anthropic API key Direct API; good if your team already uses Claude OpenAI OpenAI API key Defaults to gpt-4o-mini Google Gemini Gemini API key Defaults to gemini-2.0-flash Ollama None (self-hosted URL) For local or air-gapped deployments Enter credentials and click Save. Takes effect immediately — no server restart required. info Only admins can configure the AI provider. The Analyse with AI button is visible to all users once a provider is configured.

Click any failing test in the Launches view to open the detail panel Click Analyse with AI — analysis typically completes in 2–5 seconds depending on your provider Review: root cause category badge, confidence bar, plain-English explanation, suggested fix Optionally Confirm or Override the category to track AI accuracy over time

UReport ships a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at POST /mcp. Connect any MCP-compatible AI assistant and query your builds, test results, and pass rate trends in plain language — no browser required. MCP is not Claude-only. Any compatible client works: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Continue.dev, and others.

Step 1 — Get your API token: Click your avatar → Edit Profile → API Token → Generate Token. Step 2 — Add UReport to your MCP config (e.g. .mcp.json for Claude Code, mcp.json in Cursor): { "mcpServers": { "ureport": { "type": "http", "url": "http://your-ureport-host:4100/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" } } } } Replace http://your-ureport-host:4100 with your actual backend URL (local dev: http://localhost:4100). Step 3 — Restart your AI client. UReport tools will appear in the available tool list.

Tool Description list_presets List all saved presets. Call this first — preset names are required by list_builds and get_statistics. list_builds List recent builds matching a saved preset. search_builds List recent builds using explicit filters: product, type, version, browser, platform, team, stage. get_statistics Pass/fail counts and average pass rate for builds matching a saved preset. search_statistics Pass/fail stats using explicit filters (same shape as search_builds). get_relation_fields Discover available tags, components, teams, and custom field keys (e.g. PartnerCode, XrayId) for a product/type before filtering tests. get_tests Get individual test results for a build. Filters: status, name, tag, component, team, custom field key/value, file, path. Use custom_value alone for a broad search across all custom fields (e.g. searching for an XRAY ticket ID). The AI chains tool calls automatically — for example, it calls list_presets to get valid preset names, then list_builds to find the latest build, then get_tests to fetch failures — without you specifying IDs manually.

Assignment lets you assign failing tests to team members directly from the test list. Assignees receive an email notification, and you can send follow-up reminders when tests remain unresolved. :::warning Email Required Assignment notifications and follow-up reminders are delivered by email. If your UReport instance does not have email configured, assignees will not receive any notifications. Set up email in Administration before using this feature. :::

When a test fails, you can assign it to a specific user with a note tied to the current failure signature. If the same test fails again with the same failure in a future build, the assignment carries over automatically. If the failure changes, the assignment is no longer matched — it was for a specific failure, not the test in general. Key properties: One assignment per test per failure — creating a new assignment for the same test+failure updates the existing one instead of duplicating Assignments are scoped to a product lane (product + type) State is either OPEN or CLOSE — closing an assignment does not send a refund or notification No TTL — assignments persist until manually closed or the test is re-assigned

Right-click a failing test in the list view and select Assign. Choose a user from the search results. An email is sent to the assignee (not to yourself). The assigned test shows a user icon in the list view. Hovering reveals the assignee name.

Click the Select button (task icon) in the toolbar to enter selection mode Check the tests you want to assign — passing tests cannot be selected A floating action bar appears at the bottom Click Assign (N) → search for a user → confirm Maximum 50 tests per bulk request (backend enforced) If more than 50 tests are selected, only the first 50 are submitted.

Assignments are linked to a failure by signature, not just by test UID. When tests are loaded, each assignment is matched to a test using this priority: UID pre-filter — if both assignment and test have a UID and they differ, skip Token match — Playwright failure token (normalized — retry counts like 336 × are stripped before comparison) Stack trace match — exact stack trace (normalized) Error message match — exact error message (normalized) Normalization strips variable Playwright call-log retry counts (\d+ ×) so that 335 × waiting and 336 × waiting are treated as identical. This ensures assignments survive across builds where the retry count fluctuates. If none of the three match, the assignment is not shown on the test — it was for a different failure.
Right-click an assigned test → Unassign. This closes the assignment (state: CLOSE).
In selection mode, select assigned tests and click Unassign (N) in the action bar. Only tests with an existing open assignment are unassigned.

The Assignments page (/assignments) shows all open assignments across your lanes. You can: Filter by OPEN / CLOSE state Search by assignee username Close individual assignments The page queries the last 90 days, up to 200 results (max 500).

If assigned tests are still failing after 3 days, a banner appears at the bottom of the launches page: N assigned test(s) still failing — send a reminder? Clicking Send Follow-up opens a dialog showing each assignee and their still-failing tests. Select the assignees to notify and click Send Emails. Follow-up emails are only sent to other users — not to yourself. Eligibility rules for follow-up: Assignment must be OPEN Assignment must be at least 3 days old (assign_at ≤ now − 3 days) The test must still be failing and not investigated in the current build The failure signature must still match (same token / stack / message after normalization)

Auto-Heal detects failing tests, dispatches a repair job to an agent on your machine, applies an AI-generated code fix, verifies the fix passes, and opens a pull request — end to end, without manual steps. The Rerun feature lets you run any test on your own agent without AI involvement — useful for verifying a test locally, reproducing a flake, or running with a different environment.

License — Auto-Heal is an enterprise feature included in the same license tier as Auto-Triage. Plugin — Install the auto-heal plugin from Plugin Center before use. Agent — At least one connected agent (global or user-owned). See ureport-agent for setup.

Mode Who executes the fix Infrastructure needed When to use Guided (playbook) ureport-agent runs a fixed pipeline: checkout → AI fix → verify → open PR Install ureport-agent; configure a guided playbook Predictable, auditable pipeline with explicit steps Agent Delegation (playbook) ureport-agent hands off to Claude; Claude explores and fixes autonomously Install ureport-agent; configure a delegation playbook You want the AI agent to decide how to fix with minimal configuration External Consumer Your own system — any language, any AI, any workflow Build a poller that calls the signals API You already have an AI automation platform and want UReport to surface failures and accept outcomes. Each signal carries a full failure snapshot (error message, stack trace) and lane history so your system has everything it needs without extra API calls.

Agent mode (Guided or Agent Delegation): Failing test in a build ↓ Trigger Auto-Heal (manual or auto-trigger on build complete) ↓ Plugin creates a HealSignal (status: pending → queued) ↓ Plugin dispatches heal_job to a connected agent over WebSocket ↓ Agent runs the playbook pipeline on your machine ↓ Agent streams progress back in real time ↓ Signal updated with final status (pr_created / test_failed / bug_confirmed / error) External Consumer mode: Failing test in a build ↓ Auto-trigger fires (dispatch_mode: external in lane settings) ↓ Plugin creates a HealSignal (status: open) ↓ Your system polls GET /api/ai/heal/signals?status=open ↓ Your system claims the signal: POST /signals/:id/claim ↓ Your system processes the fix (any language, any AI) ↓ Your system reports the outcome: PUT /signals/:id Everything after the trigger is autonomous. You review the result in the Signals tab.

A connected global agent on the same server worker is used first. If none, the plugin broadcasts via cluster IPC — other workers check their global agents. If still no global agent, the triggering user's own personal agent is used as fallback. Jobs are never sent to another user's personal agent. Global agents only receive heal_job messages. Rerun jobs always go to the triggering user's personal agent — a global agent never handles a rerun.

The agent executes one job at a time — this is a global limit, not per product lane. The agent maintains a single _currentJob flag. If a second job arrives while one is running, it is dropped and stays queued in UReport until the running job finishes and the server dispatches the next one. The workspace is still organized per product lane (separate checkout directories), so multiple lanes can have their own repos cloned — but they are worked on sequentially, not in parallel.

There is no server-side queue buffer. On trigger, the server immediately tries to send the job over WebSocket. The signal status reflects what happened: Signal status after trigger Meaning queued Job sent to agent — agent has received it but not started yet no_agent No connected agent found — job was not sent Stuck signal recovery: When a global agent reconnects (sends its hello handshake), the server automatically re-dispatches all signals still in pending or queued state to that agent. This handles the case where the agent was offline when the signal was created or crashed mid-job. info User (personal) agents do not trigger re-dispatch on reconnect — only global agents do. The agent executes one job at a time. If a second heal_job arrives while the agent is busy, the agent drops it — there is no agent-side queue buffer. The signal stays queued in UReport. The server handles this in two ways: On job completion — when the agent finishes a job and sends its result, the server immediately dispatches the next oldest queued signal to the same agent. On reconnect — when an agent reconnects and sends its hello, the server re-dispatches all signals still in pending or queued state. This means triggering multiple heals in quick succession works correctly — they are processed one by one in the order they were created.

Queue limit: At most 20 signals may be in pending or queued state at once. Triggering more returns HTTP 429. Queue position: When a signal is queued, the API response includes a queuePosition field (1 = next to run). The UI displays this as Queue #N on the status badge so you can see where in line your signal is.

A server-side watchdog runs every 5 minutes. Any heal signal still in running state after 240 minutes is automatically marked timed_out. This ensures the queue never gets permanently blocked by a hung agent job.

If an agent disconnects while a job is running, the server immediately marks that signal error with the message Agent "<name>" disconnected while job was running. Other queued signals remain in the queue and are re-dispatched when the agent reconnects.
A playbook defines what the agent does when a heal job is dispatched. You configure playbooks once and reuse them across any test.

Mode Description Guided You configure a fixed pipeline of up to 4 stages. The agent executes each enabled stage in sequence. Predictable, auditable. Agent Delegation Hand off to an AI agent (Claude). Describe the goal in a prompt; the agent explores the repo and figures out how to fix the test autonomously.

Clones the repository (first run) or fetches and resets it (subsequent runs), then creates a new branch for the fix. Setting Description Git Remote URL SSH or HTTPS URL used to clone the repo (e.g. git@github.com:org/repo.git) Branch Prefix Prefix for the fix branch name (default: fix/auto-) — combined with the test name and signal ID Base Branch Branch to branch off from (default: main). If not found, the agent detects the remote default. Install Command Optional command to run after checkout (e.g. npm ci, pip install -r requirements.txt) The agent stores one workspace per product lane under repo_path: /tmp/ureport-agent-workspace/ myapp__e2e/ ← cloned for myapp / e2e lane myapp__regression/ Git credentials must already be configured on the agent machine — no credentials are stored in UReport.

Sends the failing test details to an AI model and applies the returned code changes to the workspace. Setting Description Provider claude-cli — Claude CLI (Anthropic). gemini-cli — Gemini CLI (Google). Model gemini-cli only — model flag passed to the Gemini CLI (e.g. gemini-2.0-flash). Not used for claude-cli. Instructions Prompt sent to the AI describing what to fix. Supports test variable placeholders (see below). Max Attempts How many fix+verify cycles to attempt before giving up (1–5, default 2). Each failed attempt resets changed files and retries with the previous failure output as context. Both providers run as a CLI process in the agent's workspace directory. They have native file tools to explore the repo, apply changes, run the test, and self-report whether it passed via testPassed in their JSON output. claude-cli — runs claude --print --output-format json <prompt>. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the agent machine. gemini-cli — runs gemini -p <prompt> --yolo [--model <model>]. Requires GEMINI_API_KEY on the agent machine (or authentication via gemini auth login). Authentication for AI Providers​ Provider Authentication claude-cli Browser OAuth — run claude once on the agent machine to log in. Credentials stored in ~/.claude/. No API key needed. gemini-cli GEMINI_API_KEY env var on the agent machine, or gemini auth login. Instructions Placeholders​ All placeholders are resolved by the plugin before dispatching. Placeholder Value {test.name} Full test name / title {test.file} Repo-relative path to the test file {test.uid} Test unique identifier {test.error_message} Last error message {test.stack_trace} Stack trace {test.tags} All tags, space-joined {test.tags[0]} First tag ([1] is the second, and so on; empty when there is no such tag) {test.components} All components, space-joined {test.components[0]} First component {test.teams} All teams, space-joined {test.teams[0]} First team {test.customRelation.KEY} Any custom relation field {test.info.KEY} Any raw test info field

Runs the test command after the AI fix to confirm it passes. Setting Description Test Command Shell command to run. Supports {test.file}, {test.name}, {test.uid}, {test.tags}, {test.components}, {test.teams} placeholders. Leave blank to use npm test. Environment Variables KEY=VALUE pairs (one per line) injected into the process environment. info When using Claude CLI as the AI provider, this stage is automatically skipped — Claude runs and verifies the test internally during the AI Fix stage. If the test still fails after the fix, the signal status becomes test_failed. If Create PR even if test still fails is enabled in the Create PR stage, a WIP PR is still opened with a [WIP] title prefix.

Commits the changes, pushes the fix branch, and opens a pull request. Setting Description PR Title Template Title of the PR. Supports {test.name} and other test placeholders. Default: fix: auto-heal {test.name}. Target Branch Branch the PR merges into (default: main). API Token Personal access token for the git host: GitHub (repo scope), GitLab (api scope), or a Bitbucket app password / repository access token. Stored in the playbook, not on the agent. Username Bitbucket only — required when using a Bitbucket app password. Leave blank for repository access tokens. Create PR even if test still fails Opens a [WIP] PR if the Verify stage fails. Useful to capture partial progress. The provider is auto-detected from the Git Remote URL (HTTPS, ssh:// and git@host:path forms all work). Nothing is selected in the playbook: Remote host Opens a Notes github.com GitHub pull request gitlab.com GitLab merge request Nested groups (group/subgroup/project) are supported. bitbucket.org Bitbucket Cloud pull request The repository's default reviewers are added automatically (see below). Your own GitHub Enterprise or self-managed GitLab host Same as above Add the host to git_hosts in the agent's ureport-agent.yml. See Self-hosted Git. If the remote host is not recognised, the agent stops before pushing anything and reports Unsupported git host "<host>", so no stray branch is left behind. Bitbucket Server / Data Center and Azure DevOps are not supported. Default reviewers (Bitbucket Cloud)​ Bitbucket does not add default reviewers to pull requests created through its API, so the agent looks them up (repository and project level) and adds them to the PR. You do not configure anything in the playbook. The user that owns the API token is left out, because Bitbucket does not allow the author to review their own PR. If no default reviewers are configured, or they can't be read, the PR is still created without reviewers. A reviewer problem never fails the heal. Reading default reviewers needs repository read permission on the token in addition to pull request write. Without it the agent log shows Could not read default reviewers (403) and the PR has no reviewers. GitHub and GitLab PRs are created without reviewers. The PR body includes the AI analysis, a diff summary, the original error, and a link back to the UReport signal.

In Agent Delegation mode, the playbook has a single Goal / Prompt field and a Provider setting. The agent receives the prompt along with the failing test details and autonomously explores and fixes the repo using the selected CLI tool. Provider Behavior claude-cli (default) Runs claude --print --output-format json. Has native file and shell tools. Reports testPassed in JSON output. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. gemini-cli Runs gemini -p <prompt> --yolo. Reports testPassed in JSON output. Requires GEMINI_API_KEY. If the CLI reports testPassed: true, staged changes are kept and the signal status becomes completed. If testPassed: false, the signal becomes test_failed. info Agent Delegation does not automatically commit or push — it stops at completed with staged changes. A Create PR stage is not available in this mode. The staged diff is captured and shown in the signal detail. :::warning Pre-cloned workspace required Agent Delegation skips the checkout stage. The repository must already be cloned at the expected workspace path ({repo_path}/{product}__{type}/) before the first delegation job runs. If the path does not exist, the signal immediately errors with workspace not found. Use guided mode with the Checkout stage enabled if you do not want to pre-clone manually. :::

Each Auto-Heal run creates a HealSignal that tracks progress from dispatch to outcome. Status Mode Meaning pending Agent Created, waiting to be dispatched to agent queued Agent Dispatched — agent has received it but not started running Agent Agent is actively executing the pipeline pr_created Agent Fix applied, test passed, PR opened test_failed Agent Fix applied but test still failing bug_confirmed Agent Agent determined the test reflects a real product bug (delegation mode) completed Agent Pipeline completed successfully without a PR stage error Agent Pipeline failed at a stage timed_out Agent Agent did not respond within the timeout window no_agent Agent No connected agent available at dispatch time open External Created, waiting for external consumer to claim claimed External External consumer has claimed it and is processing

Go to Tests → Auto-Heal → Playbooks tab. New Playbook — Create a new guided or agent delegation playbook (admin only). Edit — Modify an existing playbook (admin only). Delete — Permanently remove a playbook (admin only). Active toggle — Enable or disable a playbook. Disabled playbooks cannot be selected for new heal jobs. Operators can view playbooks but cannot create, edit, or delete them. In the playbook editor, Test run shows what the playbook would send to an agent for a real failing test, using your unsaved edits: your template on the left, the same text with that test's values filled in on the right. Nothing is saved or dispatched. Ready-made settings for Playwright, Jest, Vitest and Pytest are in Playbook Examples.

From the Launches page: open a build, find a failing test, click the Auto Heal button in the AI Actions bar. A dialog lets you select which playbook to use. The signal appears immediately in the Signals tab with status pending → queued as the job is dispatched. :::info Open external signal for the same test If the lane uses external dispatch and the test already has an open signal that no consumer has claimed, the manual trigger hands that signal to the agent instead of creating a duplicate (the response is 200, not 201). Two cases are refused with 409: an external consumer claimed the signal in the meantime, or no agent is connected — in that case the signal is left open for your consumer. ::: The Auto Heal button is visible when at least one agent is connected — either a global agent or your own personal agent.

Auto-Heal can fire automatically when a build completes. It runs after auto-triage so that already-triaged tests are excluded before signaling. Enable auto-trigger: Go to Tests → Settings for the product/type lane → Auto-Heal Settings. Setting Default Description Enabled off Turn on auto-trigger for this lane Dispatch Mode agent agent — dispatch to ureport-agent via WebSocket. external — create open signals for your own consumer to poll and process. Default Playbook — Playbook to use when dispatch mode is agent. Falls back to any active playbook if not set. New Failures Only on Only trigger for tests that passed in the previous build — skips known persistent failures. Max Prior Failures 3 Skip a test if it failed in this many consecutive prior builds (likely a real bug, not a flaky fix candidate). Set to 0 to disable. Exclude Quarantined off Skip tests that are currently quarantined. Max Signals per Trigger 10 Cap on how many signals to create per build completion event. Skip failures whose error message matches none List of rules. A failure whose error message matches any rule never opens a signal. Each rule is Contains, Equals or Regex; matching ignores case and looks at the error message only (not the stack trace). Example: Contains + Fail to generate token. Regex rules are checked when you save the lane, and an invalid one is skipped at run time with a warning in the server log. Applies to both dispatch modes. Manual heal from test detail is not affected. Additional instructions — External dispatch mode only. Free text copied onto every signal as additionalInstructions for your consumer to pass to its AI. Agent mode takes its instructions from the playbook. Filtering Order​ On each build completion, auto-trigger determines the final status per test UID — when a test has multiple runs (retries), only the last run counts. Then it applies these exclusions in order: Final status is not FAIL — tests that ultimately passed (including via rerun) are excluded. Error message rule — excluded if the error message matches one of the lane's "skip failures whose error message matches" rules. Active auto-triage coverage — excluded if the test has a non-expired auto-triage record (is_auto_triaged: true) and the current failure fingerprint matches the investigated pattern. See Triage exclusion rules below. Quarantined — excluded if exclude_quarantined is on and the test is currently quarantined. Not a new failure — excluded if new_failures_only is on and the test's final status in the previous build (same lane) was also FAIL. Persistent failure — excluded if max_prior_failures > 0 and the test failed in all of the last N consecutive builds. Triage Exclusion Rules​ Auto-trigger only excludes tests whose failure is actively covered by a valid auto-triage record. Manual triage records (created by a user in the UI) do not block signal creation — they are informational annotations, not active coverage gates. Condition Signal created? Reason Auto-triaged (TTL valid), current failure matches same error fingerprint No Auto-triage is actively covering this exact failure pattern Auto-triaged (TTL valid), current failure has different error fingerprint Yes New failure mode — different root cause, needs investigation Auto-triaged (TTL expired) Yes Coverage lapsed — failure is eligible again Auto-triage record missing (old records without is_auto_triaged flag) Yes Treated as expired — records from old plugin versions are not enforced Manually triaged (user-created triage in UI, any age) Yes Manual triage is a historical annotation; auto-heal signals are independent :::info Source age limit Auto-Heal reads the Source age limit from Auto-Triage Settings (same lane) to determine staleness of triage records. Auto-triage records older than this limit no longer suppress heal signals, even if their TTL has not elapsed. Records with permanent TTL (-1) are always enforced regardless of age. If Auto-Triage is not enabled or its settings have never been configured, Auto-Heal defaults to 30 days. Since only is_auto_triaged: true records can suppress heal signals, this only matters if auto-triage was previously enabled and left records behind. ::: :::warning Triage status and heal signals can coexist A test may appear as triaged in the UI (because a user manually investigated it at some point) while also having an active heal signal. This is expected behavior — the manual triage records a past investigation, and the heal signal targets the current failure which may have a different cause or occurred after the test had been passing for a while. If you want to permanently suppress heal signals for a specific test, use auto-triage with ttl: -1 (permanent coverage) rather than a manual triage. ::: Failure Grouping​ Before creating signals, auto-trigger groups the remaining candidates by error fingerprint (first stable line of error/stack trace, with line numbers and addresses stripped). One signal is created per group — the newest test in the group is the primary; the others are recorded as affectedTestUids. This prevents creating dozens of signals when a single root cause affects many tests. Dedup for external mode: if an open signal already exists for a test with the same error fingerprint, the new trigger is skipped. If the error fingerprint changed (new failure mode), the existing signal is updated with fresh build context.

Go to Tests → Auto-Heal → Signals tab. Each row shows: Test name and product lane Current status (live — refreshable) Result summary (e.g. PR branch name, error detail, bug severity) Duration from trigger to completion Trigger time Click the detail icon on any signal to open the full signal view — including per-stage output, AI analysis, the diff, test output, and history of previous signals for the same test. Admins can delete signals. Operators have read-only access.
Use this when dispatch_mode is set to external in the lane's auto-heal settings. Your system acts as the repair agent — UReport surfaces failures; your system processes them and reports outcomes.
Use a standard UReport API bearer token (same as the REST API). Pass it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Pass it to your AI along with the failure context. laneHistory Array of { buildNumber, status, startTime } for the last 10 prior builds in this lane — tells you whether this is a new regression or a recurring failure Reading laneHistory​ laneHistory is ordered newest-first. Each entry is one prior build's outcome for this test UID. "laneHistory": [ { "buildNumber": 142, "status": "PASS", "startTime": "2024-10-28T..." }, { "buildNumber": 141, "status": "PASS", "startTime": "2024-10-27T..." }, { "buildNumber": 140, "status": "FAIL", "startTime": "2024-10-26T..." } ] All recent builds PASS → this is likely a new regression introduced in the triggering build — a strong fix candidate. If the test has been rerun since then, the snapshot reflects the state when the signal was created, not the latest rerun result.
Atomically transitions the signal from open → claimed. Returns 409 if already claimed or not open. POST /api/ai/heal/signals/:id/claim { "claimed_by": "my-system-v1" }

After your system processes the fix, report the result: PUT /api/ai/heal/signals/:id Required field: status — one of pr_created, test_failed, bug_confirmed, completed, error Optional fields by status: Field When to use pr_url Required for pr_created — URL of the opened pull/merge request branch Branch name (for pr_created) diff_summary Short description of code changes applied test_output Test runner output from the verify run attempted_diff Diff that was tried (for test_failed) agent_analysis Explanation of why the fix failed or what was found bug_report Required for bug_confirmed — object with summary and optionally detail bug_tracking_url For bug_confirmed — URL to Jira/GitHub issue. UReport auto-triages affected tests with this link. error_detail Error description (for error) external_ref Any external reference (ticket ID, PR mirror URL, etc.) rerun_passed true if your system ran the test and it passed. UReport marks the test as PASS with is_rerun=true. Required (and only valid) with completed. completion_reason Optional, only valid with completed: flaky (passed on retry, intermittent) or not_reproducible (could not reproduce the failure). Shown next to the status in signal detail; put the explanation in agent_analysis. ai_provider AI provider name (informational, shown in signal detail) ai_model AI model name (informational, shown in signal detail) input_tokens Token count (informational, shown in signal detail) output_tokens Token count (informational, shown in signal detail) Auto-Triage on Bug Confirmed​ When you report status: bug_confirmed with a bug_tracking_url, UReport automatically creates InvestigatedTest records for the primary test and all affectedTestUids, linking them to the tracking URL. This prevents auto-trigger from re-signaling the same known bug on the next build.

The Rerun feature lets you run a test on your personal agent without AI involvement. It is useful for: Reproducing a failure locally Verifying a fix before committing Running with a specific environment or config Rerun jobs are always sent to your own personal agent — not a global agent. You must have a connected personal agent for rerun to work.

Before triggering a rerun, you must set up at least one Rerun Config. Go to Tests → Auto-Heal → Reruns tab. Each config defines: Field Description Name A label to identify this config (useful when you have multiple per lane) Product / Type The lane this config applies to. Multiple configs can share the same lane. Repo Mode local — agent cds into a local path. checkout — agent clones/pulls the repo. Local Path (local mode) Absolute path on the agent machine to cd into Git Remote URL (checkout mode) Remote URL to clone Base Branch (checkout mode) Branch to pull/reset to Install Command (checkout mode) Optional command to run after checkout (e.g. npm ci) Environment Variables KEY=VALUE pairs exported before the command runs. Supports placeholders. Command The shell command to run the test. Supports placeholders. Timeout Maximum minutes before the agent kills the command. Rerun configs are private — other users cannot see or use them. Placeholders​ Supported in both Command and Environment Variables: Placeholder Value {test.name} Full test name / title {test.file} Repo-relative path to the test file {test.uid} Test unique identifier {test.tags} All tags, space-joined {test.customRelation.KEY} Any custom relation field Example command: npx playwright test {test.file} --grep "{test.name}" Multiple Configs per Lane​ You can create multiple configs for the same product/type lane — for example, one for staging and one for production. When triggering a rerun with multiple configs on the same lane, a picker appears in the confirmation dialog so you can choose which config to use. Use Duplicate on any existing config to quickly create a variant.

Open any test in Launches. Click Rerun in the AI Actions bar. A dialog shows a preview of the resolved command and repo info. If multiple configs exist for this lane, select the one to use. Click Trigger Rerun. The rerun signal appears in the Reruns section of the AI Actions bar with a live status tag. If the run fails or errors, click the status tag to expand the exit code and terminal output inline.

Status Meaning pending Created, waiting to be dispatched queued Dispatched — agent has received the job running Agent is executing the command passed Command exited with code 0 failed Command exited with non-zero code timed_out Command exceeded the configured timeout and was killed error Agent encountered an error before or during execution no_agent No personal agent connected at dispatch time

Like Auto-Heal, there is no server-side queue for reruns. The job is sent immediately over WebSocket on trigger. Unlike Auto-Heal, rerun signals are not automatically re-dispatched when your agent reconnects. If your agent was offline or disconnected before picking up the job, the signal stays stuck at queued. Trigger a new rerun to retry. Scenario Result Agent connected at trigger time Signal → queued → agent picks up → running Agent offline at trigger time Signal → no_agent, not retried Agent disconnects after queued but before starting Signal stays queued — trigger a new rerun Agent disconnects while running Signal → error immediately

Queue limit: At most 5 rerun signals per user may be pending or queued at once. Triggering more returns HTTP 429. Queue position: The status badge in the AI Actions bar shows Queue #N when your rerun is waiting. Sequential dispatch: After a rerun completes, the server automatically dispatches the next pending/queued rerun for the same user to the same agent — no manual re-trigger needed.
The server-side watchdog runs every 5 minutes and marks any rerun signal stuck in running for more than 90 minutes as timed_out.

Auto-Triage automatically propagates known failure investigations to new failing tests with matching tokens, error messages, or stack traces — without any manual triage needed.

When a build completes with failing tests, auto-triage checks whether any of those failures match a known investigation — identified by failure token, error message, or stack trace. If a match is found, UReport automatically creates an investigation record for the new failing test, copying the cause and tracking number from the source. The new record is tagged as auto-triaged and has a configurable expiry (TTL) — after which the match is considered stale and the test will be re-evaluated on the next build. Auto-triage covers tests that share the same failure pattern across different test IDs, suites, or builds. Once a root cause has been investigated once, all future tests with the same failure are labelled automatically. Key properties: Fires automatically after every build completion — no action needed Copies cause and tracking info from existing investigations Message and stack trace matches expire after a configurable TTL (default 5 days); token matches and promoted matches are permanent

Auto-Triage Quarantine Purpose Label a test with a known root cause Exclude a persistently failing test from the pass rate Trigger Failure pattern match (token / message / stack trace) Failure frequency threshold (total / consecutive / rate) Effect on pass rate None — the test still counts as failed Test is excluded from the pass rate calculation Expiry Yes — auto-triage matches have a TTL No — quarantine is active until resolved or exempted Input required At least one manual investigation with a matching failure No manual input — fully rule-driven Auto-triage and quarantine can both apply to the same test at the same time. They are independent features.

Auto-triage is configured per product/type from the Launches page. Click the wand icon (✨) in the toolbar to open the auto-triage settings panel, then toggle it on. Setting Default Description Enabled Off Master switch. Auto-triage does not run unless this is on. Review TTL (days) 5 How long a message or stack trace match remains valid. After this many days, the auto-triage record expires and the test becomes eligible for re-triage. Range: 1–365. Source age limit (days) 30 Controls two things: (1) how far back to look for source investigations when matching new failures, and (2) how old an existing triage record can be before it no longer counts as active coverage — the test becomes eligible for re-triage and Auto-Heal signals. Records with permanent TTL (-1) are always covered regardless of age. Range: 1–180. :::info Source age limit vs Analysis Since Day These two settings form a hierarchy: Analysis Since Day (System Settings, global) — the overall horizon for all analysis: how far back build history, charts, and trend views can look. This is the ceiling for everything. Source age limit (Auto-Triage Settings, per lane) — a narrower, stricter subset of that horizon, applying only to automated decisions. Automated pattern matching and coverage enforcement should be conservative — using very old records risks propagating stale failure patterns as false positives. In practice, set Source age limit ≤ Analysis Since Day. For example: Analysis Since Day = 60, Source age limit = 30 means you can browse 60 days of history manually, but auto-triage and auto-heal only act on investigation records from the last 30 days. :::

Match type Expires? Default behaviour Token (token) No — permanent Never expires. Token matches are highly reliable — based on a deterministic identifier embedded in the test failure. Error message (exact) Yes Expires after Review TTL days. Stack trace (stack) Yes Expires after Review TTL days. Promoted match No — permanent A message or stack match promoted to permanent. Never expires. tip Set Review TTL to a low value (e.g. 3–5 days) for suites with dynamic error messages. Use a higher value (e.g. 14–30 days) for stable messages like assertion errors that rarely change wording.
For each failing test, auto-triage tries three lookups in priority order. The first match wins.

If the test has a failure token, it is looked up in the token map. Token matches are the most reliable — a token is a deterministic identifier generated by the test framework (e.g. a hash of the test ID + assertion location). TTL: permanent.
If no token match, the full error message is compared exactly against the message map. Punctuation, whitespace, and casing must match exactly. TTL: expires after Review TTL.

If no message match, the full stack trace is compared exactly against the stack map. Used for investigations configured with COMPARE_BY_MIXED or COMPARE_BY_STACK_TRACE. TTL: expires after Review TTL. If no match is found at any step, the test is left uninvestigated — it will be checked again on the next build.

Auto-triage builds its match maps from existing InvestigatedTest records for the same product/type, created within the source age limit window. Source type Valid as source? Notes Manual investigation, within source age limit Yes A recent human-created investigation is used as a source. Manual investigation, older than source age limit No Treated as stale — excluded from matching and coverage. Auto-triage with ttl: -1 (permanent) Always Permanent records are never considered stale regardless of age. Auto-triage, token match (within age limit) Yes Token matches are permanent — the source record never expires via TTL. Auto-triage, message/stack match (within age limit, TTL valid) Yes Included if within age limit and TTL has not elapsed. Auto-triage, message/stack match (TTL expired) No Expired via TTL — excluded from the match pool. Fuzzy match (similarity < 100%) Never Fuzzy matches cannot be safely replicated by exact lookup — always excluded. Any record older than source age limit (unless ttl: -1) No Stale — excluded from both matching and coverage checks.

An expired auto-triage record means the match confidence window has closed. Using it as a source would silently re-triage tests that should be reviewed manually — so it is excluded from the match pool. Expiry applies only to the source pool. A test that has an active (non-expired) auto-triage record is still considered investigated — it won't be re-triaged until its own TTL expires, or until the record is older than the Source age limit, whichever comes first. Records with permanent TTL (-1) never lapse.

The automatic trigger and the manual trigger use the same rule. A failing test is skipped (already investigated) when it has an investigation that is: Existing investigation Covers the test? Permanent (ttl: -1), any age Yes Manual, newer than the source age limit Yes Manual, older than the source age limit No — stale, the test can be auto-triaged again Auto-triage, TTL not elapsed and newer than the source age limit Yes Auto-triage, TTL elapsed, or older than the source age limit No
documents.s: When is a test already investigated?

documents.t: Runs automatically after every build's status calculation: Build completes — status is calculated Failing tests identified — all tests with status = FAIL are collected Rerun exclusion — tests that passed on retry (status = PASS, is_rerun = true) are excluded Coverage check — tests that already have a valid investigation are skipped (see When is a test already investigated?) Match and create — eligible tests are matched against the source pool; matches result in auto-triage records being created or refreshed Auto-triage is fire-and-forget — it never blocks the build result.

From the Launches page, click the wand icon (✨) in the toolbar to open the auto-triage panel. The panel shows how many failing tests are not yet triaged. Step 1 — Preview: Click Preview to scan failing tests against the source pool. The results table shows each match — test name, matched investigation, cause, match type, and a Permanent checkbox. No records are created yet. Step 2 — Apply: Review the matches. Check Permanent on any message or stack match you want to promote immediately. Click Apply (or Apply (N) to apply only selected rows) to create the auto-triage records. Manual trigger is useful when you just created a new investigation and want to immediately propagate it to other failing tests, or when you want to preview and selectively apply matches before enabling automatic triggering.

Promotion converts a time-limited message or stack match (TTL > 0) into a permanent one (TTL = -1). When How At apply time In the manual trigger preview table, check the Permanent checkbox before clicking Apply. Token matches are always permanent and show a lock icon instead. After creation On the Investigated Tests page, filter to auto-triaged records. Each message/stack match shows a Promote to permanent button. A Promote All button is also available per source group. A promoted record: Never expires (TTL = -1) Can serve as a permanent source for future auto-triage matches Is treated identically to a token match in terms of expiry tip Promote matches for failures caused by long-lived infrastructure issues or known external dependencies. This prevents the same investigation from needing to be re-created after the Review TTL expires.

Auto-triage skips tests with status = PASS, is_rerun = true. If a test failed but passed on retry, there is no need to propagate a prior failure investigation. Only tests that are still failing at the end of all retry attempts are candidates.

Settings: Enabled, Review TTL = 5 days, Source age limit = 90 days. Existing investigations (sources): Source UID Type Token Error message Caused by Tracking TTL checkout/pay-btn Manual — Expected element .pay-btn to be visible UI regression PROJ-1234 n/a (valid while within the source age limit) auth/login-flow Auto-triage tok_abc123 — Infra: auth service down OPS-777 -1 (permanent) search/results-count Auto-triage — AssertionError: expected 10 but got 0 Data seed missing QA-42 Expires in 3 days Build B20 fails. Failing tests after rerun exclusion: Test UID Token Error message Already investigated? cart/add-item — Expected element .pay-btn to be visible No checkout/confirm tok_abc123 — No search/pagination — AssertionError: expected 10 but got 0 No auth/logout — Timeout after 5000ms Yes (active manual) Matching: cart/add-item — no token; message matches checkout/pay-btn. Type: exact. Auto-triage created: cause = "UI regression", tracking = PROJ-1234, TTL = 5 days. checkout/confirm — token tok_abc123 matches auth/login-flow. Type: token. Auto-triage created: cause = "Infra: auth service down", tracking = OPS-777, TTL = -1 (permanent). search/pagination — no token; message matches search/results-count. Source is auto-triage with 3 days remaining — not expired. Type: exact. Auto-triage created: cause = "Data seed missing", tracking = QA-42, TTL = 5 days. auth/logout — already investigated (active manual record). Skipped entirely. After 5 days: The cart/add-item and search/pagination auto-triage records expire. On the next build where these tests fail, they are re-evaluated. If checkout/pay-btn's manual investigation still exists, is still within the source age limit (90 days here), and the error message is the same, they will be re-triaged automatically. checkout/confirm is not affected — its token match is permanent. Dashboards provide customisable views of test data using a grid of configurable widget types. Create personal or shared dashboards for single-project monitoring or cross-project comparison.

Navigate to Dashboards and click Create Dashboard Enter a name and optional description Choose visibility: Public (visible to all users) or Private (only you) Choose a Product Lane Strategy: Single Product Focus — all widgets share one product lane configured at the dashboard level. Changes to the global filter apply across all widgets simultaneously. Multi-Product Flexibility — each widget independently chooses its own product lane. Use this for cross-product or cross-team dashboards. Click Add Widget to start building — choose a widget type, configure it, and add it to the grid Dashboard layouts auto-save as you make changes. Rename a dashboard by clicking its title inline.
In a Single Product Focus dashboard, a global filter panel at the top applies across all widgets simultaneously. The filter state is preserved in the URL — bookmark or share specific views.
Product & Type (required), Team, Browser, Device, Platform, Stage, Version
Date Range, Build Range, Status Filters, Relation Filters Each widget can also have local filter overrides. Click the widget's gear icon to configure per-widget settings.
Understanding how product lanes are configured — and what happens when fields are left empty — is essential for getting accurate data in each widget.

Each widget resolves its data source in this priority order: Widget-level product lane — if the widget has its own product lane configured in the editor, that takes precedence over everything else. Only available in Multi-Product Flexibility dashboards — the Product Lane panel is hidden in Single Product Focus dashboards because all widgets inherit the dashboard-level filter. Dashboard-level query — if no widget-level override exists and the dashboard has a product lane selected (Single Product Focus), the widget inherits it. Additional lanes — a list of extra product lanes for side-by-side comparison. Can coexist with the primary lane above. Each entry fetches data independently. If none of the above is configured, the widget renders empty — it has no data source to query.

Field Required Behaviour when empty Product ✅ Yes Widget will not fetch data Type ✅ Yes Widget will not fetch data Team No Wildcard — matches builds from all teams Version No Wildcard — matches all versions Browser No Wildcard — matches all browsers Device No Wildcard — matches all devices Platform No Wildcard — matches all platforms Stage No Wildcard — matches all stages Extras No Wildcard — no extra-field filtering info Leaving an optional field empty is not the same as filtering for null — it means the field is excluded from the query entirely, so all values (including null, blank, and any non-null value) are included.

The most common configuration. Specify a product + type combination, optionally narrowed by team, stage, version, etc. The widget fetches the N most recent builds matching that filter exactly. Example: Product = Reporting, Type = API, Stage = Staging, Version = v1.2 → returns the last N builds for that exact combination. When the filter matches exactly one distinct product lane combination, the widget operates in single lane mode. :::caution Subset trap Leaving an optional field empty does not select a "parent" lane — it is a wildcard that matches all values. If you configure Product=UReport, Type=UI, Stage=Staging with Version left empty, and your data contains builds for v1.1, v1.2, and v1.3, the filter matches three distinct combinations and aggregation mode is triggered automatically. There is no way to target "all versions as a single combined lane" in single-lane mode once multiple versions exist in the data. Your options are: Specify an explicit version to stay in single-lane mode Accept aggregation mode (data pooled as Σ 0, Σ 1, … indices) Use Break aggregation (Build History Bar only) to show each version as its own independent series Use Single series (Build History Bar only) to show all matched builds as one flat chronological series :::

When you configure a product lane filter but leave one or more optional fields empty, the filter may match multiple distinct lane combinations in your data — for example, leaving Browser empty when you have Chrome, Firefox, and Safari builds all under the same product/type. UReport detects this automatically when you apply a filter. If exactly one lane combination matches, the widget shows a normal single-lane view. If more than one matches, it switches to aggregated lanes mode — all matching sub-lanes are pooled together. In aggregation mode: The chart uses Σ 0, Σ 1, … labels on the X-axis, where each index represents the Nth most recent run across all matched sub-lanes. Clicking a bar or data point opens an overlay listing each individual sub-lane build that contributed to that data point. Some widget types are hidden — Summary Card widgets and Test Analysis Table do not support aggregation and are removed from the widget type dropdown. You must configure a single-lane filter to use those widget types. Example: Product = Reporting, Type = API, Browser = (empty) — if Chrome, Firefox, and Safari builds all exist for this product/type, the widget automatically aggregates them. Impact per widget: Build History Bar — each bar represents combined counts across all matched sub-lanes for that run index Status Pie / Triaged Pie — combined test counts from the latest run across all matched sub-lanes Heatmap — each row pools tests from all matched sub-lanes for that run index Treemap / Relations Group By — tests from the latest run across all matched sub-lanes, pooled before grouping Trend Insights — trend computed from the aggregated pass rate across all matched sub-lanes Top Tests Table — unaffected; queries by product/type regardless of sub-lane count

Supported by widgets that show side-by-side comparisons (Build History Bar and Relations Group By). Add extra product lanes in the widget editor under Multiple Product Lanes. Each lane is fetched independently and rendered as a separate series. Example: Lane 1 = Chrome, Lane 2 = Firefox, Lane 3 = Safari → three independent series on the same chart. When multiple lanes are configured: A Grid View toggle appears in the widget header — shows all lanes as small charts side-by-side. A single view shows one lane at a time; use the grid view to see all simultaneously.

When aggregation mode is detected (filter matches more than one lane), the Build History Bar widget editor shows a three-option selector: Option Behaviour Aggregated (default) Builds are pooled into Σ 0, Σ 1, … run indices. Clicking a bar shows each sub-lane's contribution. Break aggregation Auto-discovers each sub-lane on every load and renders them as independent series — a special form of Multi-Lane that never hardcodes the lane list. New versions or parameter values appear automatically without re-saving. Single series All matched builds across all sub-lanes are flattened into one chronological series, one bar per actual build, sorted by start date. X-axis switches to Start Date automatically. Use this when you want a single continuous history view regardless of which sub-lane each build came from. The selector only appears when your filter matches more than one lane. For single-lane filters the widget always operates in single-lane mode and the selector is hidden. :::tip When to use Single series Choose Single series when you want to see "all staging builds, regardless of version, as one flat timeline" — for example, to spot overall quality trends without caring which version each build belongs to. Note that build numbers may collide across sub-lanes, so the X-axis defaults to Start Date. :::
documents.s: Aggregation Mode Options (Build History Bar only)

documents.t: Bar or line chart showing pass/fail/skip/triage counts across multiple builds over time. What it reads: Up to N builds (configured via range) matching the product lane, plus all tests for each build. Falls back to build-level status counts if individual test data is unavailable. X-axis options: Build Number — sequential build number Start Date — actual execution timestamp. Format is chosen automatically based on both the total number of builds and the time span they cover, so labels stay readable regardless of how dense the chart is: Builds Span Format Example > 20 any MMM dd Jun 15 > 10 or span > 10 days — MMM dd, yyyy Jun 15, 2026 ≤ 10, span > 1 day — MMM dd HH:mm Jun 15 14:30 ≤ 10, same day — MMM dd HH:mm:ss Jun 15 14:30:45 The hover tooltip always shows the full date with year and seconds regardless of the axis label format. Chart type toggle: Switch between Bar and Line at runtime. Line mode plots pass rate (0–100%) per build. Bar mode stacks pass/fail/skip/triage/outage counts. This is the same widget — the toggle is available at runtime in the widget header. Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane One series of bars/points, one per build. Aggregated lanes Each bar represents combined counts across all matched sub-lanes for that run index (Σ 0, Σ 1, …). Clicking a bar opens an overlay showing each sub-lane's contribution. Use the aggregation mode selector to switch to Break aggregation or Single series. Break aggregation Lanes auto-discovered on every load, rendered as independent series (special form of multi-lane). Lane list updates automatically as new versions appear. Single series All matched builds flattened into one chronological series sorted by start date, one bar per actual build. X-axis switches to Start Date automatically. Multi-lane Multiple independent series — one per manually configured lane. Grid view shows them side-by-side; single view shows one lane at a time. No product lane Widget shows empty — no builds to display. Analytics: When data is loaded, an Analytics overlay is available (chart icon in header). Shows pass-rate trend, build health distribution, and stability score.

Pie chart of test result distribution for the latest build only. What it reads: Tests from the single most recent build matching the product lane filter. Two modes (toggle in header): Status view — slices for Pass / Fail / Skip / Triaged (KI) / Outage Triage view — slices showing the breakdown by investigation cause (Defect, Flakiness, Environment Issue, etc.) Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane Shows status distribution of the latest build in that lane Aggregated lanes Combines tests from the latest run of each matched sub-lane. Pie reflects the totals across all groups. Multi-lane Not applicable — Status Pie does not support multi-lane. Configure separate widgets per lane. No product lane Widget shows empty. Triage view note: Issue type colours come from your Settings → Issue Types configuration. Up to 5 types are shown as individual slices; remaining types are grouped into "others".

Identical to Status Pie Chart but opens on the Triage view by default — slices show the breakdown by investigation cause (Defect, Flakiness, Environment Issue, etc.) rather than run status. All product lane scenarios and behaviour are the same as Status Pie Chart.

A compact card grid showing key metrics. A single widget can display three different card sets — switch between them at runtime using the selector at the top: Build Summary​ Counts and buckets all builds in the configured range by pass rate: Bucket Range 🏆 Perfect 100% ✅ Good 90–99% ✅ Acceptable 80–89% ⚠️ Warning 60–79% ❌ Poor 40–59% 🚫 Critical below 40% Also shows average pass rate with a trend indicator (↑ / ↓) comparing the first half to the second half of the build range. Status Summary​ Aggregates test counts across all builds in the range (not just the latest). Shows executed total, pass, fail, skip, triaged, and outage. Also shows an "active" count (executed minus skipped/outaged) when relevant. Triaged Summary​ Shows triage coverage across all builds: total triaged tests, new triage (first analysed in the current build) vs carried over (auto-matched from a previous triage). Breakdown by issue type using your configured issue type colours. Product lane scenarios (applies to all three card types): Scenario Behaviour Single lane Metrics computed from builds in that lane over the configured range Aggregated lanes Not supported — Summary Card widgets are hidden from the widget type dropdown when your filter matches multiple lane combinations. Configure a single-lane product filter to use these widgets. No product lane Widget shows empty.

Colour-coded matrix: rows represent builds (newest at top), columns represent values of a relation dimension. Cell colour encodes pass rate — green (high) to red (low). What it reads: N builds and all tests per build, then groups tests by the selected relation dimension (component, team, tag, or custom field). Configuration: Group By — select which relation dimension to use as columns (configured in widget editor; can be changed at runtime via the selector in the widget header) Build range — how many builds (rows) to show Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane One row per build, one column per relation value Aggregated lanes Each Σ index becomes a row; tests from all matched sub-lanes are pooled before grouping No product lane Widget shows empty. Clicking a cell opens a detail drawer listing the individual builds that contributed to that cell, with links to launch the test view for that specific build.

Hierarchical visualisation of test distribution across a relation dimension. Block size is proportional to test count; colour encodes pass rate. What it reads: Tests from the latest build, grouped by the selected relation dimension. Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane Tests from the latest build in that lane Aggregated lanes Tests from the latest run of each matched sub-lane, pooled together No product lane Widget shows empty. Clicking a block navigates to the Launches view filtered to that relation value.

Stacked bar chart grouping tests from the latest build by a relation dimension. Each bar represents one relation value; segments show pass/fail/skip/triage breakdown. Modes: Horizontal bars Vertical bars Table — tabular view with pass rate column Multi-lane support: Relations Group By supports Multiple Product Lanes (same as Build History Bar). Add extra product lanes in the widget editor to show side-by-side comparisons across lanes. Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane Groups tests from the latest build Aggregated lanes Groups tests from the latest run across all matched sub-lanes Multi-lane Multiple independent series — one per configured lane No product lane Widget shows empty.

Tabular analysis of test behaviour patterns across all builds in the configured range. Classifies each test as: Stable — consistently passes across builds Unstable — passes in some builds, fails in others (flaky) Consistently failing — fails in most or all builds Shows flakiness percentage, total runs, and fail count per test. Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane Analyses tests across the configured build range for that lane Aggregated lanes Not supported — Test Analysis Table is hidden from the widget type dropdown when your filter matches multiple lane combinations. Configure a single-lane product filter to use this widget. No product lane Widget shows empty. Supports CSV export of the full table.

Ranked table surfacing the most impactful tests. Unlike most widgets, this widget queries an analytics API over a time window rather than a build range. Two modes (toggle at runtime): Mode Shows Top Failures Tests that failed most frequently; columns: fail count, last failed date Slowest Tests Tests with the longest average duration; columns: avg duration, max duration, run count Time window options: Last 7 days / 30 days / 90 days (configurable in the widget header at runtime). Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane Top tests within that product/type (and any optional filters) over the time window Aggregated lanes The widget remains available and queries the analytics API using the configured product/type filter. Because the analytics API is time-window based (not build-pipeline based), results reflect all data matching the product/type regardless of multi-lane configuration. No product lane Widget shows empty.

Detects anomalous pass-rate drops across recent builds using Z-score analysis. What it reads: Pass rates across the last N builds (default 20). Computes a statistical baseline and flags builds where the pass rate deviated significantly. Overlays: Pass rate timeline with anomaly markers Build duration trend — reveals if the suite is getting slower over time Product lane scenarios: Scenario Behaviour Single lane Trend analysis for that lane Aggregated lanes Trend computed from the aggregated pass rate across all matched sub-lanes No product lane Widget shows empty.

Visual separator that organises dashboard content into logical sections. Customisable title, colour, font size, and line style Enables jump-to-section navigation when multiple dividers are present Spans full dashboard width Does not fetch any data — no product lane configuration needed

Each widget has specific configuration options accessible via the gear icon: Setting Description Widget Title Custom label for the widget header Product Lane Selection Which product lane(s) the widget queries. Only shown in Multi-Product Flexibility dashboards — in Single Product Focus dashboards, widgets inherit the dashboard-level filter and this setting is hidden. See Product Lane Configuration above. Date Range Overrides dashboard-level date range for this widget Build Range Number of recent builds to fetch (default: 20) Status Filters Which statuses to include in calculations Relation Filters Pre-filter tests by relation dimension values before the widget processes them Chart Type / Visual options Widget-specific display settings (axis label, direction, colours, layout)

Widgets that support multi-lane (Build History Bar and Relations Group By) can compare data from multiple product lanes side-by-side: Open the widget editor Expand Multiple Product Lanes Click Add Product Lane to add additional data sources — configure each with a different filter combination Use arrow buttons to reorder lanes; edit or remove as needed Use cases: Cross-Browser — Chrome, Firefox, Safari lanes side-by-side Team Performance — Frontend, Backend, QA team lanes Environment — Dev, Staging, Production comparison The Multiple Product Lanes section only appears for widgets that support it.

Feature Description Public dashboards Visible to all logged-in users Private dashboards Only accessible to the creator Clone dashboards Create a personal copy of any dashboard URL sharing Direct links with embedded filter state — shareable and bookmarkable PDF Export Full-page PDF snapshot of the current dashboard view CSV Export Raw data export from the Test Analysis Table widget
