documents.t: UReport supports two authentication methods: API Token (recommended for CI/scripts) Generate a personal API token: avatar → Edit Profile → API Token → Generate Token. Include in every request: Authorization: Bearer <your-api-token> Session Cookie (browser / interactive) Call POST /api/login with username and password. The response returns a sessionId. Send it as a cookie in subsequent requests: Cookie: connect.sid=<sessionId> info For automated pipelines pushing test results, API token + Authorization: Bearer is the cleanest approach. Reporter plugins handle this automatically when you provide the token in the config.

Check the response body for specific error messages about which fields are invalid. Required fields for builds: product (string, required) type (string, required) Required fields for tests: build_id (string, required) name (string, required) status (string, required)

Refresh the page — a simple refresh often resolves transient rendering issues. Clear browser cache — clear cache and reload to get latest assets. Check widget size — some charts need minimum dimensions; try resizing the widget larger.
Check your profile settings and verify the selected theme. Clear browser cache to ensure latest styles are loaded. Check browser extensions — dark mode extensions can interfere with the app's theme.

Reporting a bug — include: Steps to reproduce Expected vs actual behaviour Browser and OS information Screenshots if applicable Requesting a feature — describe: The problem you're trying to solve Your proposed solution How it would benefit your workflow ← Administration

ureport-agent is a lightweight Node.js process that runs on your machine (or CI server). It connects to UReport over WebSocket, receives heal and rerun jobs, executes them in your local repository, and streams progress and results back.

Node.js 18+ Git configured with push access to your repository (SSH key or HTTPS credentials) — required for Auto-Heal checkout stage AI provider key — GEMINI_API_KEY for gemini-cli. claude-cli authenticates via browser OAuth (~/.claude/ config) — no API key needed. The auto-heal plugin must be installed on the UReport server

Go to My Agent (/agent) in UReport. Click Download .tar.gz (macOS/Linux) or Download .zip (Windows). Extract the archive: tar -xzf ureport-agent.tar.gz cd ureport-agent No npm install needed — production dependencies are bundled.

Copy ureport-agent.yml.example to ureport-agent.yml and fill in your values: # ── Required ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ureport_url: https://your-ureport-server agent_token: YOUR_TOKEN_HERE # Root workspace — agent stores per-lane repos here repo_path: /tmp/ureport-agent-workspace # ── Optional ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Max minutes to wait for a single claude --print invocation (default: 30) # claude_cli_timeout_minutes: 30 # Max minutes to wait for a single gemini -p invocation (default: 30) # gemini_cli_timeout_minutes: 30 # Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise / GitLab (see "Self-hosted Git" below) # git_hosts: # git.mycompany.com: # provider: github # ── Security (all optional, see "Security Options" below) ───────────────────── # signing_secret: your-secret-here # allowed_run_prefixes: # - npx playwright test # - npm test # accept_job_types: # - heal # - rerun # audit_log: ./ureport-agent-audit.log

Field Required Default Description ureport_url Yes — Full URL to your UReport server (no trailing slash). HTTP and HTTPS both supported. agent_token Yes — Agent token generated from the UReport UI. repo_path No ./workspace Root directory where the agent clones repositories. One subdirectory per product lane. claude_cli_timeout_minutes No 30 Maximum minutes to wait for a single claude --print invocation to complete. gemini_cli_timeout_minutes No 30 Maximum minutes to wait for a single gemini -p invocation to complete. git_hosts No — Maps self-hosted git hostnames to a provider so the Create PR stage can open PRs there. See Self-hosted Git. signing_secret No — Shared secret used to verify that jobs really come from your UReport server. See Security Options. allowed_run_prefixes No — List of command prefixes the agent may run for Verify and Rerun. Anything else is blocked. accept_job_types No heal, rerun Job types this agent accepts. Set to one value to restrict the agent. audit_log No — File path. When set, the agent appends one JSON line per job received, rejected, blocked and finished.

The Create PR stage works with github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org out of the box. For a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise or self-managed GitLab, tell the agent which provider a hostname uses: git_hosts: git.mycompany.com: provider: github gitlab.mycompany.com: provider: gitlab api_url: https://gitlab.mycompany.com/api/v4 Field Required Description (key) Yes Hostname exactly as it appears in the playbook's Git Remote URL, without a port. provider Yes github or gitlab. api_url No API base URL. Defaults to https://<host>/api/v3 (GitHub) or https://<host>/api/v4 (GitLab). Set it explicitly if the server uses a custom port or path. Notes: This is configured on the agent machine only, never in the playbook. The playbook's API token is sent to the API host configured here, so it is deliberately not something a playbook can change. An invalid entry stops the agent at startup with invalid config: git_hosts.<host>: .... Bitbucket Server / Data Center and Azure DevOps are not supported.

All four are optional and independent, and the agent works with none of them set. They protect the machine the agent runs on, because the agent executes commands from jobs sent by the server. Setting When not set signing_secret Every job is accepted, with no signature check. allowed_run_prefixes Any Verify or Rerun command is allowed (command substitution is still blocked). accept_job_types Both heal and rerun jobs are accepted. audit_log No audit log is written. There is no default file. signing_secret — verify jobs come from your server When set, the agent only runs a job whose message carries a valid HMAC-SHA256 signature made with the same secret. The server signs jobs with the HEAL_SIGNING_SECRET environment variable, so both must hold the same value: signing_secret: a-long-random-string A job with a missing or wrong signature is rejected and logged (invalid signature). Leave signing_secret out and the agent accepts every job, as before. If you set it on the agent but not on the server, every job is rejected. allowed_run_prefixes — limit what commands can run allowed_run_prefixes: - npx playwright test - npm test Applies to the commands the agent runs for the Verify stage and for Rerun. If a command does not start with one of the prefixes, it is blocked and the job reports the reason. The check is a plain "starts with" match. It does not stop a command from chaining more commands after an allowed prefix (for example npm test && other-command), so treat it as a guard against mistakes and unexpected commands, not as a sandbox. It does not apply to the playbook's Install Command or to the AI provider's own actions in the workspace. Leave it out and any Verify or Rerun command is allowed. Commands containing a backtick or $(...) (command substitution) or a null character are always blocked, with or without this setting. accept_job_types — restrict what the agent does accept_job_types: - rerun Allowed values are heal and rerun. The default is both. A job of a type that is not listed is ignored and logged. Use it, for example, to make a shared CI machine run reruns only. The agent also reports its accepted types to the server when it connects. audit_log — keep a record of what ran audit_log: ./ureport-agent-audit.log The agent appends one JSON object per line. A relative path is resolved against the folder you start the agent from. event When Other fields job_received A job passed the checks and was accepted type, signal_id, mode (heal jobs) job_rejected Invalid signature, or job type not in accept_job_types reason, signal_id command_blocked A Verify or Rerun command failed the allowlist stage, reason, cmd job_result The job finished type, signal_id, status Every line also has a ts ISO timestamp. If the log can't be written, the agent prints a warning and keeps running. The file is never rotated or trimmed by the agent.

Variable When Required GEMINI_API_KEY Any playbook using the gemini-cli provider claude-cli does not use an API key — it authenticates via browser OAuth. Run claude once on the agent machine to log in; credentials are stored in ~/.claude/. Set these in your shell environment before starting the agent, or use a process manager that injects them.
There are two types of agent tokens, each for a different purpose:

Generated by any user from the My Agent page (/agent). Used for: Rerun — when you trigger a rerun on a test, the job is sent exclusively to your own agent. Auto-Heal fallback — if no global agent is connected, Auto-Heal falls back to your personal agent. Each user can have one personal agent token at a time. Regenerating replaces the previous token and disconnects the existing agent.

Generated by admins from the Global Agents tab on the Auto-Heal page. Used for: Auto-Heal — the plugin routes heal jobs to any connected global agent first. Multiple global tokens can exist simultaneously (e.g. one per CI runner or machine). The plugin picks a connected one at dispatch time.

Personal token: Go to My Agent (/agent). Click Generate Agent Token. Give it a name (e.g. My MacBook, CI Runner). Copy the token — shown only once. Store it in ureport-agent.yml. Global token (admin only): Go to Tests → Auto-Heal → Global Agents tab. Click Generate Token. Copy and configure on the agent machine.

cd ureport-agent node agent.js To use a config file at a custom path: node agent.js /path/to/ureport-agent.yml On startup, the agent logs its version, server URL, and workspace path: [agent] ureport-agent v0.2.1 [agent] server: https://your-ureport-server [agent] workspace: /tmp/ureport-agent-workspace [agent] connecting to wss://your-ureport-server/ws/agent [agent] connected [agent] registered as: My MacBook

The agent opens a persistent WebSocket connection to {ureport_url}/ws/agent using its token as a Bearer header. On connect, it sends a hello message with its version. The server registers it and sends back registered. The agent sends a ping every 30 seconds to keep the connection alive. If the connection drops for any reason, the agent waits 5 seconds and automatically reconnects — no manual restart needed.

Auto-Heal jobs (heal_job): Plugin looks for a connected global agent on the worker that handled the HTTP request. If none found locally, broadcasts via cluster IPC — other workers check their connected global agents. If still no global agent, falls back to the triggering user's own personal agent (same two-step process). Jobs are never sent to another user's personal agent. Rerun jobs (rerun_job): Always sent exclusively to the triggering user's personal agent. Global agents never receive rerun jobs. If the user has no connected agent, the rerun signal is created with status no_agent.

The agent executes one job at a time — a single global flag, not per lane. If a second job arrives while one is running, the agent drops it; the signal stays queued and is dispatched again when the current job finishes. Progress messages are streamed back in real time and visible in the signal detail view.

The agent creates subdirectories inside repo_path: /tmp/ureport-agent-workspace/ myapp__e2e/ ← Auto-Heal guided: workspace for myapp / e2e lane myapp__regression/ ← Auto-Heal guided: workspace for myapp / regression lane rerun__<key>/ ← Rerun (checkout mode): separate workspace per rerun config Auto-Heal guided/delegation: one directory per product+type lane (product__type). Cloned on first run; fetched and reset on subsequent runs; a new fix branch is created each time. Rerun (checkout mode): directory named rerun__<key> based on the test UID. Cloned on first run; fetched and reset to base branch on subsequent runs. No new branch — runs directly on base. Rerun (local mode): no workspace created — the agent cds into the configured local path as-is.

The My Agent page (/agent) shows the connection status of your agent: Status Meaning Connected Agent is connected and ready to receive jobs Disconnected Agent has connected before but is not currently connected Never Connected Token exists but the agent has never connected Admins see a Global Agents tab (all global tokens and their status) and a User Agents tab (all user-owned agents).

To keep the agent running in the background and restart on failure, use a process manager. pm2: npm install -g pm2 pm2 start agent.js --name ureport-agent pm2 save pm2 startup systemd (Linux): [Unit] Description=ureport-agent After=network.target [Service] WorkingDirectory=/opt/ureport-agent ExecStart=/usr/bin/node agent.js Restart=always # Environment=GEMINI_API_KEY=your-key ← only needed for gemini-cli playbooks [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target

config not found: ureport-agent.yml Copy ureport-agent.yml.example to ureport-agent.yml and fill in ureport_url and agent_token. replace PASTE_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE with a real token Generate a token from the UReport My Agent page and paste it into ureport-agent.yml. Auto-Heal signal stays no_agent No connected agent was available at dispatch time. Either connect a global agent (Admin → Auto-Heal → Global Agents) or connect your personal agent. Global agents are preferred; your own personal agent is used as fallback. Rerun signal stays no_agent Rerun jobs are sent only to your personal agent. Go to My Agent (/agent), generate a token, and start the agent with it. heal_job REJECTED — invalid signature signing_secret in ureport-agent.yml does not match HEAL_SIGNING_SECRET on the UReport server, or only one of them is set. Make both the same value, or remove signing_secret from the agent. Verify or Rerun reports command does not match any allowed prefix The command does not start with any entry in allowed_run_prefixes. Add the prefix to the list or change the command in the playbook. GEMINI_API_KEY env var not set Set GEMINI_API_KEY in the shell environment before starting the agent (only needed for gemini-cli playbooks). checkout.remote is not set in the playbook Add a Git Remote URL to the Checkout stage in the playbook configuration. PR creation fails with GitHub API 422 The fix branch may already exist remotely from a previous run. Delete the stale branch from GitHub or change the branch prefix in the playbook. The same applies to GitLab and Bitbucket errors about an existing branch or merge request. Unsupported git host "<host>" The remote URL's host is not github.com, gitlab.com or bitbucket.org. For a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise or GitLab, add the host to git_hosts in ureport-agent.yml (see Self-hosted Git) and restart the agent. The check runs before anything is pushed. No git remote found. Set the repo URL in the playbook's Checkout settings. The Create PR stage found no repository URL. Set Git Remote URL in the playbook's Checkout stage. Bitbucket PR created without reviewers Check the agent log for Could not read default reviewers. The token needs repository read permission as well as pull request write, and default reviewers must be configured on the repository or its project. Agent did not call finish() within turn limit Agent Delegation hit the 20-turn limit without completing. Use a more specific prompt, or switch to Guided mode for predictable pipelines.
